results.evidence: Git ignored local.prod under local.[!e]*, while collectSourceArtifactFiles included it.

A bare deploy was accepted, stripped environments, and retained the staging principal in top-level constants. That unrelated principal then read victim-production-secret through the resulting read:* role on the production target app.
The unrelated attacker claimed the released label before the documented new-app claim.
The pinned origin gate accepted reclaimed.bounded.page for victim-app after the host map identified attacker-app, because the victim allowlist remained stale.
The pinned sanitizer retained both /reset/Reset_A7b9 and Authorization: Bearer sk-audit-only-123456.
After an unrelated victim added 10000000 units of collateral, a future-dated market accepted creator outcome NO and an immediate 20000000-unit sweep, leaving collateralReserve 0 before expiry.

An unrelated attacker bought 5000000 YES, then two distinct sell paths in one accepted setMany each paid the 10000000-unit pre-state quote. The physical payout was 20000000, draining the creator's 10000000-unit seed, while the final recorded reserve was 10000000.

After an unrelated victim's bet, the policy accepted two attacker bets. Three unsettled 100000000-unit bets against a 500000000-unit pot created 600000000 units of maximum payout liability and a 100000000-unit shortfall.

The pinned implementation recomputes both quote and minimum from execution reserves. The code-level proof moved the quote from 90 with a signed-time minimum of 85 to an accepted execution quote of 23 with a recomputed minimum of 21.
The documented rewrite evaluated true where the intended inequality evaluated false for spent=1, scale=100, tokens=50, price=1. Severity and reproducible agent-causality gates remain separate.
Following the base-unit instruction with a six-decimal token magnified 1000000 caller units to 1000000000000 transferred base units. Reachability and attacker-control gates remain separate.

The pinned /agents/* admission path accepts any verified app JWT and forwards the verified identity without a role or action authorization decision. A distinct lower-privileged wallet invoked the deployed documented kind: agent handler on the local stack, mutated its app-scoped runtime store, and caused the handler to receive a declared audit-only app secret. The same user's direct policy write was denied, and a runtime ctx.bounded attempt was also denied by the downstream policy, confirming that policy rules remain a defense for that surface. The pinned Flue environment additionally exposes services, queues, schedules, and app-service data capabilities to the resulting tool loop; the complete public guidance provides no agent/onInvoke authorization gate and limits its warning to kind: backend fetch handlers.

The pinned NFT runtime sets the invoking wallet as payer, supplies a destination owner, and omits authority and update_authority in the standalone branch. Cargo.lock pins mpl-core 0.10.0, whose create contract test proves that an omitted standalone update authority defaults to the payer, contradicting the documented program-managed authority guarantee. A focused policy using the public mintNFT signature without a collection passed the pinned CLI's solana_devnet deploy-safety gate with zero schema or proof failures.
